Job 14:17), but so that he utterly forgets them, so that they perish and never come into God's reckoning for ever, and so that, by looking upon them, he would not condemn the sinner. And, suppressed, subdued, and cast into the depths of the sea (Mic. 7:19), they are wholly deprived of the power to accuse and condemn the sinner.

units.la: XXXIV. Hæc autem valida peccatorum absconsio à conspectu Dei judicis id omne non est, quod duplici hac phrasi, claudendi & obsignandi, significatur. Verum amplius modus, quo id fieri debet, declaratur, nempe interposito quodam operculo seu tegumento inter peccata & faciem summi Judicis, quo clausa, recondita, & in æternum remota essent ab illius vultu. Quod redemtionis nostræ mysterium præfiguravit olim Deus operculo propitiatorio, quod ex ejus mandato Arcæ supernè impositum erat, ad tegendas Legis tabulas, in ipsa Arcæ cavitate sepositas; Et pones אל הארן in arcam Testimonium ( tabulas legis 1 Reg. viii. 8. Heb. ix. 4.) quod dabo tibi. Et pones את הכפרת operculum propitiatorium super arcam superne, & in arcam pones Testimonium, quod dabo tibi. Et conveniam te illic, & loquar tecum desuper è propitiatorio, è medio duorum Cherubinorum, quod est super Arca Testimonii. Exod. xxv. 16. 21. 22. Habitabat Deus inter Cherubinos, unde præsentiam suam gratiosam certis quibusdam signis & responsis manifestabat Israeli. Hoc autem non decebat Deum, nisi lex, officii quidem norma, sed & transgressionis index, peccatoremque accusans & condemnans, tecta esset operculo quodam, & quidem propitiatorio, quod nempe sanguinem adspersionis adjunctum haberet, quo posset placare Numen, etiam cum Testimonio istius legis. Illud vero operculum aureum, sanguine animalium brutorum conspersum, id, quod lex postulat à peccatore, præstare non poterat ad placandum Numen; cujus sanctitas, justitia, veritas, longè aliud placamentum exigebant. Præfigurabat itaque aliud operculum, ipso auro infinities præstantius; alium Mediatorem, non brutorum, sed suo ipsius infiniti valoris sanguine conspersum, in quo Deus secum mundum reconciliaret, & qui δικαίωμα legis impleret, ut peccatum condemnaretur. Hic autem est Filius Dei JESUS CHRISTUS, Mediator Dei & hominum, quem προέθετο ante tempus, vel ante faciem hominum, posuit Deus ἱλαστήριον operculum propitiatorium, per fidem, in sanguine ipsius Rom. iii. 25.
units.tr: XXXIV. This strong concealment of sins from the sight of God the judge is not all that is signified by this twofold expression, closing and sealing. Rather, it further declares the manner in which this must be done: namely, by placing a certain covering or veil between sins and the face of the supreme Judge, by which they would be shut up, hidden, and removed for ever from his countenance. God long ago foreshadowed this mystery of our redemption by the mercy seat, which by his command was placed above the Ark, to cover the tables of the Law laid up in the very hollow of the Ark. "And you shall put in the ark the testimony" (the tables of the law, 1 Kings 8:9; Heb. 9:4) "which I shall give you. And you shall put the mercy seat above the ark, and in the ark you shall put the testimony which I shall give you. And there I will meet with you, and I will speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are upon the ark of the testimony" (Exod. 25:16, 21, 22). God dwelt among the cherubim, whence he made known his gracious presence to Israel by certain signs and answers. Yet this would not have befitted God, unless the Law, which indeed is the rule of duty but also the index of transgression, accusing and condemning the sinner, were covered by a certain covering, namely a mercy seat, which had sprinkled blood joined to it, by which the Deity could be appeased even in the presence of the testimony of that law. But that golden covering, sprinkled with the blood of brute animals, could not do what the law demands of the sinner, in order to appease the Deity, whose holiness, justice, and truth demanded a very different atonement. Therefore another covering was foreshadowed, far more excellent than the gold itself: another Mediator, sprinkled not with the blood of brute beasts but with his own blood of infinite worth, in whom God reconciles the world to himself, and who fulfils the righteous requirement [δικαίωμα] of the law, so that sin is condemned. This is the Son of God, JESUS CHRIST, the Mediator between God and men, whom God "set forth [προέθετο] before" the time, or "before" the face of men, as "a propitiatory [ἱλαστήριον] mercy seat, through faith, in his blood" (Rom. 3:25).

units.la: XXXV. Adeò multa in Christo conspicienda meditanda ac credenda sunt fidelibus, ut integer sacerdotii Levitici tici apparatus necessarius fuerit, ad cognitionem quandam my-steriorum, quæ in ipso recondita sunt, dandam Israeli. Sacer-dotes, altaria, victimæ ipsæ, umbræ erant ejus, qui simulsa-cerdos, qua Immanuel, victima, quoad humanitatem, & al-tare foret, quad Deitatem. Mensa cum panibus propositio-nis in Sancto collocata ipsum delineabat, qui panis vitæ est, & simul mensa, in qua quæri & inveniri is debet & potest. In Sancto Sanctorum Manna, Virga Aaronis, ipsa Arca integra, & speciatim Operculum ei super impositum, vario respectu figu-ræ Christi fuerunt. Quæ omnia latius exequi institutum no-strum non patitur. Hoc solum monendum censemus, quod Lex Arcæ inclusa alium respectum induat, si Christum subima-gine Arcæ integræ, quam si eundem sub similitudine operculi Propitiatorii concipiamus. Priori nempe modo significabatur studium Legis, quod in Christo perfectissimum ac exactissimum foret. Quorsum alluditur Psal. xl. 9. Facere voluntatem tuam Deus mi delector, ותורתך בתוך מעי & lex tua in medio visce-rum meorum est. Posteriori modo Lex consideratur ut pecca-tum monstrans, eique vim peccatorem accusandi & condem-nandi concilians; δύναμις δὲ ἁμαρτίας ὁ νόμος, 1 Cor. xv. 56. Hoc pacto Lex dum consideratur, Christus illud Operculum est propitiatorium, quod præstando id, quod lex exige-bat, sanguinem proprium fundendo, Deique iram in corpore & anima sustinendo, implevit δικαίωμα τοῦ νόμου, eique & pec-catis os obturavit, eaque coercuit, arctissimeque conclusit, ne amplius eum, qui in Christo est, peccatorem condemnare va-leant, eumque execrationi subjicere & a Dei gratiosa & gloriosa communione arcere queant 2 Cor. v. 18. 12. Rom. viii. 1. 3. Gal. iii. 13. 1 Cor. xv. 55. 56. 57. 1 Joh. ii. 2. &c. Huc respicit Psaltes, Beatus, cujus tectum est peccatum Ps. xxxii. 1. Abstulisti iniquitatem populi tui, texisti omne peccatum eorum, Selah. Psal. lxxxv. 3. Huc & respicit Deus in hoc nostro textu, quando peccata Claudenda & obsignanda pronunciat.
units.tr: XXXV. So many things in Christ must be observed, meditated upon, and believed by believers, that the whole apparatus of the Levitical priesthood was necessary to give Israel some knowledge of the mysteries hidden in him. The priests, the altars, and the sacrifices themselves were shadows of him who would at once be the priest, as Immanuel; the victim, as to his humanity; and the altar, as to his deity. The table with the showbread set in the Holy Place portrayed him who is the bread of life, and at the same time the table at which he ought and may be sought and found. In the Holy of Holies, the manna, the rod of Aaron, the Ark itself entire, and especially the mercy seat placed upon it, were figures of Christ in various respects. Our plan does not allow us to pursue all these at length. We think only this should be noted: that the Law enclosed in the Ark takes on a different aspect if we conceive of Christ under the image of the whole Ark, and if we conceive him under the likeness of the mercy seat. In the former way what is signified is the study of the Law, which in Christ would be most perfect and most exact, to which Psalm 40:9 alludes: "I delight to do your will, O my God," and "your law is within my bowels" [ותורתך בתוך מעי]. In the latter way the Law is considered as showing sin and giving it power to accuse and condemn the sinner: "the power of sin is the law" [δύναμις δὲ ἁμαρτίας ὁ νόμος] (1 Cor. 15:56). When the Law is considered in this way, Christ is that mercy seat, which, by doing what the law required, shedding his own blood and bearing God's wrath in body and soul, fulfilled "the righteous requirement [δικαίωμα] of the law," and stopped the mouth of sin, restrained and tightly shut it up, so that it can no longer condemn him who is in Christ as a sinner, subject him to the curse, or keep him from the gracious and glorious communion of God (2 Cor. 5:18; Rom. 8:1, 3; Gal. 3:13; 1 Cor. 15:55-57; 1 John 2:2, etc.). The Psalmist looks to this when he says, "Blessed is he whose sin is covered" (Ps. 32:1), and "You have taken away the iniquity of your people, you have covered all their sin, Selah" (Ps. 85:3). God also looks to this in our present text, when he pronounces that sins are to be shut up and sealed.

units.la: XXXVI. Sapientissimo profecto consilio hæc ita ef-feruntur.
units.tr: XXXVI. Certainly these things are set forth by a most wise plan.

units.la: Inter alia, quibus Templum secundum caruit, à Judæis constanter numeratur etiam Arca cum Propitiatorio. Defectum cjus umbratilis Operculi abundè compensandum fore missione Christi veri Propitiatorii, in consolationem fidelium promittit Deus. Præterea, die quovis Expiationis, cum sanguine Pontifex summus adytum ingrediebatur, eoque ipsum operculum inspergebat, & hoc pacto ei vim, ad legem & peccatum claudendum, semper de novo conciliabat; imo hoc sanguine quasi sigillo, operculo impresso, peccatum ac legem obsignabat, ac valide occludebat coram Dei, Cherubim inhabitantis, facie & aspectu. Hujus umbræ veritatem in Christo fore conspiciendam, in fine lxx. hebdomadum, in Jubileo spirituali, ac die Expiationis vero, prænunciat Deus elegantissime. Nempe tum sanguine conspergendus erat Christus proprio, cujus virtute ἱλαστήριον factus peccata obsignaret, oculosque Dei ab iis plane averteret, ne intueri iniquitatem in Jacobo, neve perversitatem aspicere in Israele posset Num. xxiii. 15. adeo ut, si quaeratur iniquitas Israelis, nulla extaret, & peccata Jehudæ, nulla inventurentur Jer. l. 20. utpote virtute lapidis illius fundamentalis, prius rudius per passiones excisi, dein sculptura elegantiori per gloriam secutam expoliti, è conspectu Dei, uno quidem die, remota Zach. iii. 9. Et sic quidem, ut eorum amplius, exactione etiam chirographi, non recordaretur Deus Jer. xxxi. 34. Heb. viii. 12. x. 17. 18.
units.tr: Among the things the Second Temple lacked, the Jews constantly count the Ark with the Mercy Seat. God promises that the lack of its shadowy cover would be abundantly made up by the sending of Christ, the true Propitiatory [ἱλαστήριον], for the comfort of believers. Moreover, on every day of Atonement, when the high priest entered the inner sanctuary with blood, he sprinkled the cover itself with it, and in this way he always renewed its power to shut up the law and sin. Indeed, with this blood, as with a seal pressed on the cover, he sealed sin and the law and firmly shut them up before the face and gaze of God, who dwells between the cherubim. God most elegantly foretells that the truth of this shadow would be seen in Christ at the end of the seventy weeks, in the spiritual Jubilee, and truly on the Day of Atonement. For then Christ was to be sprinkled with his own blood, and by its power, made a propitiatory, he would seal up sins and utterly turn the eyes of God away from them, so that God could not "see iniquity in Jacob, nor behold perverseness in Israel," Num. xxiii. 15; so that, "if Israel's iniquity is sought, none will be found, and Judah's sins will not be found," Jer. l. 20. He would be like that foundation stone, first roughly cut by sufferings and then polished with finer carving by the glory that followed, removed from the sight of God in one day, Zech. iii. 9. And so God would no longer remember their sins, not even by exacting the handwriting, Jer. xxxi. 34; Heb. viii. 12; x. 17, 18.

units.la: XXXVII. Suppositum ita de hisce rebus differentes, ipsum Operculum sanguine olim conspersum fuisse. Operæ pretium erit hanc hypothesin paululum illustrare ac confirmare.
units.tr: XXXVII. Having thus spoken of these matters on the assumption that the Mercy Seat itself was once sprinkled with blood, it will be worth while to illustrate and confirm this hypothesis a little.

units.la: In Cod. Joma. Cap. iv. dicitur, quod Pontifex non intueretur ad spargendum sursum aut deorsum. Verba hæc sunt. Nec intuebatur ad spargendum sursum aut deorsum. Ad quæ verba Sheringhamius. Non intuebatur in propitiatorium; neque enim opus erat, cum sanguis, ut in Gemara traditur, in terram lapsus sit, & ad propitiatorium non pervenerit. Confirmat hanc glossam ex Bartenora, cujus verba latine hunc in modum exhibet. Non intuebatur ad spargendum, non sursum, ut esset sparsio una in fastigio propitiatorii, & septem deorsum in medio ejus, quia supra propitiatorium non pervenerint, sed in terram deciderint. Nos secus sentimus. Verba textus sic se habent. Et accipiet de sanguine juvenci illius, & spargeт digito suo super faciem Propitiatorii, orientem versus; & coram propitiatorio spargeт, septem vicibus de illo sanguine digito suo. עַל־פְּנֵי הַכַּפֹּרֶת קֶדְמָה וְלִפְנֵי הַכַּפֹּרֶת Deum Sponsorem acceptasse, & victimam in locum peccatoris surrogasse, in cujus oblatione olim futura hactenus acquiescceret, in fide offerentibus peccata remitteret, mundum reliquum tolerare, externaque beneficia Israeli conferret, & corporales etiam plagas sisteret Num xvi. 46. 47. Gen. viii. 21. Sic nihil consummavit Lex, sed fuit ἐπεισαγωγὴ κρείττων ἐλπίδος Heb. vii. 19. ac signum & sigillum expiationis verae, per melius sacrificium perficiendae, quam hic ut futuram igitur Deus promittit.
units.tr: In the Mishnah, tractate Yoma, chapter iv., it is said that the high priest did not look up or down when sprinkling. The words are: "Nor did he look while sprinkling upwards or downwards." On these words Sheringham comments: "He did not look at the Mercy Seat; for there was no need, since the blood, as the Gemara relates, fell to the ground and did not reach the Mercy Seat." He confirms this gloss from Bartenora, whose words he gives in Latin in this way: "He did not look while sprinkling, not upwards, so that there would be one sprinkling on the top of the Mercy Seat and seven downwards in its middle, because they did not reach above the Mercy Seat but fell to the ground." We think otherwise. The words of the text are as follows: "And he shall take of the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it with his finger upon the face of the Mercy Seat eastward; and before the Mercy Seat he shall sprinkle seven times of that blood with his finger" [Lev. xvi. 14]. [Hebrew: עַל־פְּנֵי הַכַּפֹּרֶת קֶדְמָה וְלִפְנֵי הַכַּפֹּרֶת]. God had accepted the Surety, and had put the victim in the place of the sinner; in the offering of which he had hitherto been content, that in faith he might forgive the sins of those offering, bear with the rest of the world, and bestow outward benefits on Israel, and even stay bodily plagues, Num. xvi. 46, 47; Gen. viii. 21. Thus the Law accomplished nothing, but was "a bringing in of a better hope" [ἐπεισαγωγὴ κρείττων ἐλπίδος], Heb. vii. 19, and a sign and seal of true atonement, to be perfected by a better sacrifice, which God therefore promises as future here.

units.la: XL. Facta est ergo haec expiatio iniquitatis per Filium Dei in plenitudine temporis manifestatum in carne, Jesum Christum. Huic, quod olim in victimis, maximeque in hirco distincta ceremonia praefiguratum fuit Levit. xvi. 21. 22. impósita & imputata sunt peccata nostra, ab ipso sponsione aeterna voluntarie suscepta. Quae imputatio peccatorum, eorumque in se susceptio causa est, quod sponsor vocetur Heb. vii. 22. quod peccata nostra sua dicat Ps. xl. 13. lxix. 4. 5. quod olim dicere potuerit מצאתי כפר inveni redemtionis pretium Iob. xxxiii. 22. 23. & quod cum ipse innocens in se & sanctissimus fuerit, tanta mala, caelitus immissa, in corpore & anima sustinuerit; quod alias salva Dei Patris sanctitate, justitia, veritate, bonitate, absque hac peccati imputatione fieri non poterat. Agit Messias de hac susceptione Ps. lxix. 10. conf. Rom. xv. 3. Uti autem ut victimae piaculari imputata ipsi peccata nostra sunt, ita & propter ea traditus, vulneratus, crucifixus, mortuus est Rom. iv. 25. Iesf. liii. 4. 5. 6. 8. & factus est pro nobis, ut olim victimae loco offerentis, אשם Iesf. liii. 10. ἁμαρτία 2 Cor. v. 21. execratio Gal. iii. 13. quando peccata nostra sursum ipsemet, sacerdos & victima, in corpore suo tulit super lignum 1 Pet. ii. 24. Quod autem sanguis mille arietum olim efficere non valebat, nisi in imagine, id Christus unica oblatione sui ipsius confecit. Inde veniens in mundum prius illud abstulit, ut posterius statueret Heb. x. 9. ex Ps. xl. 8. 9. Expiavit peccatum & delevit, quod hactenus extabat in tabulis summi Creditoris, δι' ἑαυτοῦ καθαρισμὸν ποιησάμενος τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν consedit ad dextram majestatis in altissimis Heb. i. 3. εἰς ἀθέτησιν ἁμαρτίας per immolationem sui ipsius factus manifestus Heb. ix. 26 adde Heb. ix. 15. Colos. ii. 14. Atque ita unica oblatione τετελείωκε consummavit mavit in perpetuum eos, qui sanctificantur, impetrata actu remissione peccatorum, ita ut & memoria eorum & recordatio, tanquam nondum expiatorum, pereat Heb. x. 14.17. Hæc illa expiatio vera & consummata est, die expiationis vero conficienda; heic promissa; qua semel facta sacrificiis & sanctuario terrestri amplius locus esse nec poterat nec debebat.
units.tr: XL. This atonement for iniquity was therefore made through the Son of God, manifested in the flesh in the fullness of time, Jesus Christ. Upon him, as was foreshadowed in the victims, and above all in the goat, in the distinct ceremony, Lev. xvi. 21, 22, our sins were laid and imputed, which he voluntarily took upon himself from the eternal surety-ship. This imputation of sins and his taking them upon himself is the reason why he is called "surety," Heb. vii. 22; why he calls our sins "his own," Ps. xl. 13; lxix. 4, 5; why he could once say, "I have found a ransom" [מצאתי כפר], Job xxxiii. 22, 23; and why, although he was himself innocent and most holy, he endured such great evils, sent from heaven, in body and soul. Otherwise, with the holiness, justice, truth and goodness of God the Father left intact, this could not have been done without the imputation of sin. The Messiah speaks of this taking upon himself in Ps. lxix. 10; compare Rom. xv. 3. And just as our sins were imputed to him as to the expiatory victim, so he was also delivered, wounded, crucified and died on account of them, Rom. iv. 25; Isa. liii. 4, 5, 6, 8; and he was made "for us," in the place of the offerer, as once the victim was, [אשם] Isa. liii. 10; [ἁμαρτία] 2 Cor. v. 21; a curse, Gal. iii. 13, when he himself, priest and victim, "bore our sins in his own body on the tree," 1 Pet. ii. 24. What the blood of a thousand rams could not accomplish, except in an image, Christ accomplished by his single offering of himself. Hence "coming into the world, he took away the first, that he might establish the second," Heb. x. 9, from Ps. xl. 8, 9. He made atonement for sin and blotted out what had hitherto stood in the books of the supreme Creditor; "having by himself made purification of our sins" [δι' ἑαυτοῦ καθαρισμὸν ποιησάμενος τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν], he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high, Heb. i. 3; "to put away sin" [εἰς ἀθέτησιν ἁμαρτίας] by the sacrifice of himself he was made manifest, Heb. ix. 26; add Heb. ix. 15; Col. ii. 14. And so, by one offering he has "perfected for ever" [τετελείωκε] those who are sanctified, the forgiveness of sins being actually obtained, so that their memory and recollection of them, as of sins not yet atoned for, perishes, Heb. x. 14, 17. This is that true and completed atonement, to be accomplished on the Day of Atonement, promised here; once it was made, there could be and ought to be no further place for sacrifices and the earthly sanctuary.

units.la: XLIII. Narrant Judæorum Magistri, quod Summus Sacerdos linguam coccineam, quæ lanei staminis erat, rubro tincta, alligaverit die Expiationis ad caput hirci Emissarii, & quod quando hircus ille de rupe <bl>עזאזל</bl> dejiciebatur, ea colorem exuerit purpureum, nativamque albedinem induerit, in certum expiationis præstitæ testimonium.
units.tr: XLIII. The teachers of the Jews relate that on the Day of Atonement the high priest tied a scarlet thread, which was of woollen yarn dyed red, to the head of the scapegoat, and that when that goat was cast down from the cliff of Azazel [עזאזל], the thread lost its purple colour and took on its natural whiteness, as a sure testimony that atonement had been made.

units.la: Quod ut rite animadvertere posset hirci illius ductor, linguam coccineam dividebat, dimidium ejus ad rupem, dimidium vero inter hirci cornua alligabat, ne, si tota ad frontem hirci appensa fuisset, contingeret forte, ut qui hircum duceret nesciret aliquando an albuisset: quia dum hircus præceps ferebatur, cum reliquum corpus instar velaminis capiti obtenderetur, linguam coccineam tegi necesse erat. Addunt autem, postremis temporibus Templi secundi, & quidem quadraginta annis ante destructionem Hierosolymorum, contigisse, ut lingua illa coccinea non exalbesceret; quod iræ Divinæ, & non factæ expiationis per Pontificem Maximum, argumentum erat. Quæ si vera sunt, perhibent Judæi testimonium contra se ipsos, & testimonium dant inscii & inviti expiationi factæ per sacrificium Jesu Nazareni, quem crucifixerunt, eodem ferme tempore, quando lingua illa coccinea, juxta ipsos, in rubedine suâ manebat. Interfecto enim Filio Dei, gravissimi sceleris reatum sibi contraxerunt Judæi, ob quod iram suam sic ostendisse Deum singulari & gravioris judicii insecuturi documento, ipsimet sic fatentur. Et quando Pontifex futurorum bonorum, sui ipsius oblatione, expiaverat omnia omnium sibi datorum peccata, haud mirum erat, quod lana illa rubra in rubedine sua manserit; factum id est, ut significaretur frustra Judæos hircorum sanguine quærere peccatorum suorum expiationem. Quicquid sit de hac traditione Judaica, eatenus eam contra Judæos recipimus, quatenus expiationem hanc, in fine 490 annorum futuram, eodem prædicti temporis articulo factam esse ostendit. Dubitant tant cæteroquin Viri Doctissimi, an hæc ita se habuerint, uti Judæi fabulantur; quamvis illi, ne videantur absque ullo fundamento ex Scripturis Sacris hæc tradere, confugiant ad locum Ief. 1. 18. quasi ibi allusio esset ad ritum hunc, & mirabilem rubræ lanæ in albam mutationem. Ita quæritur in Mischna, Tractatu Schabbath. Unde habemus, quod alligare debuerint linguam coccineam capiti hirci emissarii? Ex eo, quod dictum; si fuerint peccata vestra sicut dibapha, sicut nix dealbabuntur. Vid. Spencerum de Hirco Emiss.
units.tr: So that the leader of that goat could properly observe this, he divided the scarlet thread: half he tied to the rock, and half between the goat's horns, lest, if the whole thread had been hung on the goat's forehead, the one leading the goat might by chance not know whether it had turned white; for while the goat was being hurled headlong, and the rest of its body was held over its head like a veil, the scarlet thread had to be covered. They add that in the last times of the Second Temple, and indeed forty years before the destruction of Jerusalem, it happened that this scarlet thread did not turn white, which was a sign of divine wrath and of atonement not made by the high priest. If these things are true, the Jews bear witness against themselves, and unwittingly and unwillingly bear witness to the atonement made by the sacrifice of Jesus of Nazareth, whom they crucified, at about the same time when, according to them, that scarlet thread remained red. For after the Son of God had been killed, the Jews incurred the guilt of a most grave crime, and by this they themselves confess that God showed his anger by a singular and heavier judgment as a warning. And since the High Priest of good things to come, by his own offering, had atoned for all the sins of all given to him, it is no wonder that the red wool remained red; this happened to signify that the Jews sought in vain the atonement of their sins by the blood of goats. Whatever may be the case with this Jewish tradition, we accept it against the Jews only so far as it shows that this atonement, to be made at the end of the 490 years, was made at the very time predicted. Otherwise learned men doubt whether these things happened as the Jews relate; although, lest they seem to pass these things on without any basis in the Holy Scriptures, they take refuge in Isa. i. 18, as if there were an allusion there to this rite and the wonderful change of red wool into white. So it is asked in the Mishnah, tractate Shabbath: "Whence do we have that they were bound to tie a scarlet thread to the head of the scapegoat? From what is said: 'If your sins are like scarlet [dibapha], they shall be made white as snow.'" See Spencer, on the scapegoat.

units.la: XLIV. Verum non sufficit ad peccatoris salutem liberare ipsum à reatu & pœna peccati, nisi simul ipsi adducatur jus vitæ æternæ, & communio Dei, à qua per peccatum excidit, cujusque spem amisit.
units.tr: XLIV. Yet it is not enough for the sinner's salvation that he be freed from the guilt and punishment of sin, unless at the same time the right to eternal life is brought to him, and communion with God, from which he fell through sin and whose hope he has lost.

units.la: Unde ut perfectum Salvatorem Christum describens Angelus, ei porro tribuit justitia æterna adductionem. Vox justitia notat in sacris eam rectitudinem cogitatorum dictorum factorumque, quâ cum legis postulato exacte conveniunt. Ita Paulus vocem δικαιοσύνην, quæ convenit cum Hebr. צדק & צרקה / sumit Rom. x. 5. Moses enim describit justitiam, quæ est ex lege, quod qui fecerit ea homo vivet per illa. Hæc prima vocis notio est, ex qua cæteræ fluunt, quando pro statu absolutionis à crimine, vel jure ad vitam æternam sumitur Ief. LIV. 17. Prima hac notione hic etiam vox sumenda est, quando & reliquæ nominatæ non excluduntur. Intelligimus nempe per justitiam hanc, non aliqualem, sed perfectissimam omnibusque numeris absolutam legis obedientiam, quæ præstita est causa peccatori, cujus peccata expiata sunt, juris ad vitam æternam. Qualis justitia cum nullibi hactenus reperta fuerit, nec apud homines omnes peccato coinquinatos inveniri potuerit, merito eam adducendam, id est præstandam, & actu sistendam loco & bono peccatoris declarat Angelus. Ita & frequenter Prophetæ de justitia hac, ut futura, loquuntur Pf. LXXXV. 11. Pf. XL. 10. Nec silent iidem per quem hæc justitia foret adducenda Ier. XXIII. 5. 6. XXXIII. 15. 16. Ief. XLV. 24. adde Dan. IX. 25. Ief. LIII. 11. Hæc justitia revelatur Euangelio Rom. I. 17. III. 21. & monstratur esse in Jesu Nazareno nostro, vero Davidis Germine. Hic adduxit justitiam, quam prædixerunt vates. Omnem enim justitiam implevit Matth. III. 15. omneque postulatum legis, quæ sancit chacharitatem erga Deum & proximum, præstitit, per sanctitatem naturæ integram, à primâ conceptione conservatam, & succesivam sanctitatis in rectissimis cogitatis dictis & factis omnibus expressionem accuratissimam & constantissimam Pf. xlv. 8. Isef. liii. 9. Luc. i. 35. Heb. vii. 26. 2 Cor. v. 21. 1 Petr. ii. 22. iii. 18. Joh. viii. 46. Neque hoc tantum sed & speciali mandato Patris, de ponenda vita suâ pro peccatoribus, summa cum lubentia se subjecit, obediens factus Patri usque ad mortem crucis Joh. x. 18. Pf. xl. 8. 9. Joh. iv. 34. Phil. ii. 7. 8. Atque hæc ejus perfectissima justitia, etiam in passionibus & morte demonstrata, causa est omnis justitiæ peccatoris, qua absolvitur à reatu mortis æternæ, & jus gloriæ cælestis ipsi addicitur Isef. xlv. 24. 25. Ier. xxiii. 6. Rom. v. 17. ii. 19. &c. Est enim absolutissima, adeoque vi verborum, quæ qui fecerit illa, vivet per illa, debet esse causa juris ad vitam, peccatori fideli. Peccatori, inquam, seu nobis: nam Christus fuit Servus Jehovæ justus, ac per obligationem fœderalem, naturali, qua hominis, superadditam, ut secundus Adam, Caput & Sponsor electorum legi subjectus fuit; ut adeo quicquid egerit & passus fuerit, id omne nostro nomine & loco factum sit. Optimè hæc Christi justitia, ut causa juris ad vitam, cum expiatione peccati jungitur, quia hæc ab illa separari non potest. Ad expiationem enim requiritur victima pura & immaculata, id est, passio cum perfectissimâ obedientiâ juncta. Deinde etiam præter expiationem peccatorum, ad plenitudinem salutis nostræ requirebatur meritum obedientiæ consummatissimæ, quo multi constitueremur justi, & ad certam vitæ spem & possessionem deduceremur. Et hinc loquitur Angelus de justitia adducenda, quæ passionibus demonstrata, sic faceret ad expiationem peccati, ut simul esset causa juris ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: Hence the Angel, describing Christ as the perfect Saviour, ascribes to him further the bringing in of everlasting righteousness. In the Scriptures the word righteousness denotes that rectitude of thoughts, words and deeds by which they agree exactly with what the law requires. So Paul takes the word δικαιοσύνην [dikaiosynēn], which corresponds to the Hebrew צדק [tsedeq] and צרקה [tsedaqah], at Rom. 10:5: Moses describes the righteousness which is of the law, that the man who does those things shall live by them. This is the first meaning of the word, from which the others flow, when it is taken for the state of absolution from guilt, or for the right to eternal life, as at Isa. 54:17. In this first sense the word is also to be understood here, since the other meanings are not excluded. By this righteousness we understand not some partial obedience but the most perfect obedience to the law, absolute in every respect, which was rendered in the place of the sinner, whose sins were expiated, and which gives a right to eternal life. Since such righteousness has never been found anywhere so far, nor could it be found among men all defiled with sin, the Angel rightly declares that it is to be brought in, that is, to be performed, and actually set forth in the place and for the good of the sinner. So too the prophets often speak of this righteousness as future: Ps. 85:11; Ps. 40:10. Nor do the same prophets fail to name the one through whom this righteousness was to be brought in: Jer. 23:5-6; Jer. 33:15-16; Isa. 45:24; add Dan. 9:25; Isa. 53:11. This righteousness is revealed in the Gospel, Rom. 1:17; 3:21, and is shown to be in Jesus of Nazareth, our true offspring of David. He brought in the righteousness which the prophets foretold. For he fulfilled all righteousness, Matt. 3:15, and rendered every requirement of the law, which enjoins love towards God and neighbour, through an entire holiness of nature, preserved from the first conception, and a continual and most constant expression of holiness in all most upright thoughts, words and deeds: Ps. 45:8; Isa. 53:9; Luke 1:35; Heb. 7:26; 2 Cor. 5:21; 1 Pet. 2:22; 3:18; John 8:46. Nor only this, but in obedience to the special command of the Father to lay down his life for sinners, he submitted himself with the greatest willingness, becoming obedient to the Father even unto the death of the cross: John 10:18; Ps. 40:8-9; John 4:34; Phil. 2:7-8. And this his most perfect righteousness, shown also in his sufferings and death, is the cause of all the righteousness of the sinner, by which he is absolved from the guilt of eternal death and the right to heavenly glory is assigned to him: Isa. 45:24-25; Jer. 23:6; Rom. 5:17; 5:19, etc. For it is most absolute, and so, by the force of the words the man who does those things shall live by them, it must be the cause of a right to life for the believing sinner. For the sinner, I say, or for us: for Christ was the just Servant of Jehovah, and, by a covenant obligation added to his natural human condition, he was made subject to the law as the second Adam, the Head and Surety of the elect; so that whatever he did and suffered, it was all done in our name and place. This righteousness of Christ, as the cause of a right to life, is rightly joined with the expiation of sin, because the two cannot be separated. For expiation requires a pure and spotless victim, that is, a passion joined with the most perfect obedience. Moreover, besides the expiation of sins, the fullness of our salvation required the merit of the most complete obedience, by which many are made righteous and led to the sure hope and possession of life. And hence the Angel speaks of righteousness to be brought in, which, shown in the sufferings, would so make expiation for sin that at the same time it would be the cause of the right to eternal life.

units.la: XLV. Non debet præteremitti, quod hæc justitia dicatur עולמים seculorum, id est, æterna.
units.tr: XLV. It must not be passed over that this righteousness is called עולמים [olamim], of ages, that is, eternal.

units.la: Non solum ita dicitur à posteriori, quia in æternum efficax est ad justificandum, & ipsa justificatio ex ea profluens irrevocabilis est Rom. viii. 30. Justitia autem mea in seculum erit Jef. li. 8. 6. Sed etiam à priori, quia ab æterno, cum Christo προεγνωσμένου nobis destinata est, ab omni ævo promissa, ut vid.mus, & vis ejus, in temporis plenitudine demum præstitæ retroacta sit ad justifistificandum Patres, à mundi initio promissionem de Semine benedicente fide ampleƈtenes Rom. iv. 3. 6. 7. 8. Gal. iii. 6. 8. Gen. xv. 6. Quæ rationes cum solidæ satis sint, non est, quod Osiander in hac appellatione justitiæ æternæ errori suo, de justitia essentiali Filii Dei intelligenda, prætextum quærat.
units.tr: It is called so not only a posteriori, because it is effective for justification for ever, and the justification that flows from it is irrevocable: Rom. 8:30; But my righteousness shall be for ever, Isa. 51:8. It is also so called a priori, because from eternity it was appointed for us, foreknown [προεγνωσμένου, proegnōsmenou] by Christ, promised from every age, as we have seen; and its power, though at last brought into effect in the fullness of time, was carried back to justify the Fathers, who from the beginning of the world embraced by faith the promise of the blessed Seed: Rom. 4:3, 6-8; Gal. 3:6, 8; Gen. 15:6. Since these reasons are sufficiently solid, there is no need for Osiander to seek a pretext in this expression righteousness of the ages for his error, that it is to be understood of the essential righteousness of the Son of God.

units.la: XLVI. Pulcherrimè heic rursus alluditur ad diem Expiationis, qui est in anno Jubileo. Uti enim die illo, quo proclamabatur annus Jubileus, expiatio universalis typica peragebatur, ita in fine earum hebdomadum expiationem veram & actualem futuram esse modo vidimus. Jam pergimus observantes, quod, uti ipso die Expiationis anni Jubilei, non solum peccata expiabantur, sed simul libertas servis, & possessio domuum, fundorum &c. reddebatur absque ullo pretio iis, qui egestate coacti ea vendiderant Levis xxv1. ita etiam in fine harum hebdomadum simul cum expiatione peccati adducta est justitia Christi, cujus beneficio peccatori egeno acquisitum est jus ad hæreditatem cœlestem, & ut ex servitute Diaboli & peccati ad familiam paternam cœlestem transeat. Huc respicitur Jes. lxi. 1. 2. 3. & 10. Uti verò sic redditæ possessiones tempore Jubilei postea rursus alienari poterant, ita heic contrarium promittitur, nempe justitia ÆTERNA.
units.tr: XLVI. Here again there is a most beautiful allusion to the Day of Atonement, which falls in the Jubilee year. For just as on that day, on which the Jubilee year was proclaimed, a universal typical expiation was performed, so at the end of those weeks we have just seen that a true and actual expiation was to come. Let us go on, observing that just as on the very Day of Atonement of the Jubilee year not only were sins expiated, but at the same time liberty was restored to slaves, and possession of houses and fields and so on was returned without any price to those who had been forced by poverty to sell them (Lev. 25), so also at the end of these weeks, together with the expiation of sin, the righteousness of Christ was brought in, by whose benefit a right to the heavenly inheritance was acquired for the needy sinner, and he might pass from the slavery of the devil and sin into the heavenly paternal family. To this refers Isa. 61:1-3 and 10. But just as lands restored in the time of Jubilee could afterwards be alienated again, so here the opposite is promised, namely ETERNAL righteousness.

units.la: XLVII. Hæc peccati expiatio, justitiæque æternæ adductio, vaticiniis de illâ antiquis fidem conciliabat. Idcirco additur; Ad obsignandum visionem & prophetam. Inter alios revelationis divinæ modos est etiam nin. Ea revelatio divina, quæ obtingebat homini vigilanti ; sive exhibito ei obječto externo, additisque verbis, rerum futurarum prænunciis, quibus externi ejus sensus visus & auditus afficiebantur; sive magis absque sensuum externorum ope, repræsentatione rei futuræ menti facta, vel verbis auditis vel emblematibus visis φαντασίων, strictè dicebatur visio. Cujus nomenclationis ratio peti potest à visis plerumque emblematibus, operatione facultatis intellectualis, claritateque ac certitudine revelationum apud Vates. Ita strictè sumitur visio, distincta ab simili revelatione, quam dormientes in insomnis nanciscebantur Num. xii. 6. Joel. ii. 28. Dan. i. 17. Iob. v. 14. Exempla ejus sunt Exod. iii. 3. Dan. x. 7. Jes. vi. 1. 2. Ezech. i. & iv. & 12. 15. &c. Cæ-teroquin latius etiam nomen visionis de revelatione facta in somno usurpatur Dan. VII. I. 11. 28. Imo omnis fere visio, sive antecedenter, sive concomitanter, sive consequenter, soporem quendam junctum habuit ac ecstasin Gen. XV. 12. Dan. X. 9. Act. 9. 10. 11. Apoc. I. 17. Et quia hic revelationis modus valde frequens erat, inde est, quod prophetae non solum Videntes Ham. VII. 12. 2. Sam. XV. 27. Isef. XXIX. 10. &c. dicti sint, sed etiam communiter omnis revelatio divina visionis nomen sortita sit Pf. LXXXIX. 20. Thren. II. 9. Isef. I. 1. Obad. I. 1. Prov. XXIX. 18. Quomodo & hcic vox sumenda est, notans adeo, no tam ipsum revelationis actum divinum, quam quidem ipsas res visas, & ex revelatione Dei praedictas a Viris Dei, scriptoque comprehensas; conf. Ezech. VII. 27. Dan. X. 14. 2. Chron. XXXII. 32.
units.tr: XLVII. This expiation of sin and bringing in of everlasting righteousness made faith in the ancient prophecies concerning it agree. Therefore it is added: To seal up the vision and the prophet. Among the other modes of divine revelation is also the vision [חזון, chazon]. That divine revelation which came to a man awake, whether an external object was presented to him with added words foretelling future things, by which his external senses of sight and hearing were affected, or rather without the aid of the external senses, when the representation of a future thing was made to the mind, either by words heard or by emblematic appearances seen [φαντασιῶν, phantasiōn], was strictly called a vision. The reason for this name may be sought in the emblems that were mostly seen, in the working of the intellectual faculty, and in the clarity and certainty of the revelations among the prophets. In this strict sense vision is taken, distinct from the similar revelation which those asleep received in dreams: Num. 12:6; Joel 2:28; Dan. 1:17; Job 5:14. Examples of it are Exod. 3:3; Dan. 10:7; Isa. 6:1-2; Ezek. 1 and 4, and 12, 15, etc. Otherwise the name of vision is also used more widely for a revelation made in sleep: Dan. 7:1, 11, 28. Indeed almost every vision, whether before, during or after, had a certain accompanying sleep or ecstasy: Gen. 15:12; Dan. 10:9; Acts 9:10-11; Rev. 1:17. And since this mode of revelation was very frequent, it is why the prophets were not only called seers, 2 Sam. 15:27; 2 Sam. 7:12; Isa. 29:10, etc., but also every divine revelation commonly received the name of vision: Ps. 89:20; Lam. 2:9; Isa. 1:1; Obad. 1:1; Prov. 29:18. In this way the word is to be taken here as well, denoting not so much the divine act of revelation itself as the very things seen and foretold by the men of God through the revelation of God and comprised in writing: cf. Ezek. 7:27; Dan. 10:14; 2 Chron. 32:32.

units.la: XLVIII. Visioni ideoque jungitur נביא Haec vox non incommode à נוא deducta notat generaliter eum; ad quem Deus venit, ei se familiarirer patefaciendo, arcanaque sua revelando; quique rursus ad Deum venit, precibus Gen. XX. 7. sacrisque canticis Exod. XV. 20. 1 Sam. X. 5. nomen ejus celebrando; Deique porro nomine ad homines venit, ex ejus ore accepta verba de rebus arcanis elocuturus, venturaque sequentibus aevis praenunciaturus, προφήτης. Ier. XXIII. 22. 28.
units.tr: XLVIII. The word נביא [nabi] is joined to vision. This word, not unsuitably derived from the root נבא [naba], generally denotes one to whom God comes, making himself familiarly known to him and revealing his secrets; and who in turn comes to God with prayers (Gen. XX. 7.) and sacred songs (Exod. XV. 20.; 1 Sam. X. 5.), celebrating his name; and who then comes in God's name to men, to speak in words received from his mouth about hidden things and to foretell things to come in later ages: a prophet [προφήτης] (Jer. XXIII. 22, 28.).

units.la: Quae postrema vocis notio inde à temporibus Samuelis magis frequens fuit, uti colligunt eruditi ex 1 Sam. IX. 9. Ea & heic obtinet. Perinde jam est, an per prophetam intelligas prophetiam, id est praedictiones prophetarum, an vero scripta eorum, quibus eae asservantur Luc. XVI. 29. res enim eodem redit, nempe visionem & prophetam denotare praedictiones videntium prophetarum de rebus futuris, olim prolatas, literisque consignatas. Nisi velimus cum Clar. Coccejo visionem paulo latius sumere, atque referre etiam ad praedictionem typicamque praemonstrationem rerum futurarum, quae fuit in umbris ceremoniisque Legis Mosaicae; ita ut visio & propheta hic fere idem sit ac Lex & propheta Matth. XI. 13. Verba ejus sunt Obsignabitur visio & Propheta, hoc est quicquid de salute per figuras fuit adumbratum & prophetas praedictum, id verificabitur Quaest. Jud. cap. LII. 43. Quod amplius ex expiatione peccati, in qua est veri ficatio umbrarum, praemissa, atque hinc fluente cessa-tione tione sacrificii & muneris, vers 27. hujus Capitis memorata, con• firmare annititur, in Comment. ad Hab. cap. 11. Dubito an vox visionis ullibi tam late sumatur, dum rem ipsam heic saltem consequenter propositam libenter concedo. Cæterum observandum est, quod non omnes prædictiones de quibuscunque rebus futuris sed illæ modo intelligendæ sint, quæ de occlusione obsignat one & expiatione peccati, æternæque justitiæ adduetione, unctione denique Sanctissimi, id est de Christo venturo, passuro, resurrecturo, adscensuro, agunt, quæque satis numerosæ utramque prophetarum paginam faciunt, ac intra Lxx. septimanas completæ sunt. Unde apparet error Viri Docti, qui omnes prophetias omnium prophetarum heic intelligit, licet nobis cum videatur agnoscere, prophetias has intra definitum tempus Lxx. hebdomadum obsignandas esse. Qui error altero illo cumulatur, juxta quem omnes prophetias ad Templum Secundum restringit, atque eo adhuc stante vel pereunte finiri dicit.
units.tr: This latter meaning of the word became more frequent from the time of Samuel, as scholars gather from 1 Sam. IX. 9. It holds here too. It makes no difference whether by prophet you understand prophecy, that is, the predictions of the prophets, or rather their writings, in which these are preserved (Luke XVI. 29.); for the matter comes to the same thing, namely that vision and prophet denote the predictions of seeing prophets about future things, once uttered and committed to writing. Unless we wish, with the learned Coccejus, to take vision somewhat more broadly and to refer it also to the typical foreshowing and prediction of future things, which lay in the shadows and ceremonies of the Mosaic Law; so that vision and prophet here is almost the same as Law and prophets (Matth. XI. 13.). His words are: The vision and the Prophet shall be sealed; that is, whatever about salvation was foreshadowed through figures and foretold by the prophets, that will be verified (Quaest. Jud. cap. LII. 43.). He strives to confirm this further from the expiation of sin, in which the shadows are verified, which precedes, and from the consequent cessation of sacrifice and offering, mentioned in verse 27 of this chapter, in Comment. ad Hab. cap. II. I doubt whether the word vision is anywhere taken so broadly, though I willingly grant the thing itself, at least as it is here consistently proposed. Moreover, it must be observed that not all predictions of whatever future things are to be understood, but only those which deal with the sealing up of sin and its expiation, the bringing in of eternal righteousness, and finally the anointing of the Most Holy, that is, with the Christ who is to come, to suffer, to rise and to ascend; these make up a sufficiently large part of both pages of the prophets and were fulfilled within the seventy weeks. Hence the error of the learned man is evident, who understands here all the prophecies of all the prophets, although he seems to us to acknowledge that these prophecies are to be sealed within the defined time of seventy weeks. This error is compounded by that other one, according to which he restricts all prophecies to the Second Temple, and says that they are finished while that temple still stands or perishes.

units.la: L. Visiones hasce propheticas obsignandas porro dicit Angelus. Variâ notione hæc obsignandi vox venit, pro vario sigilli & obsignationis usu & fine. Literæ jam finitæ obsignari solent; unde obsignare idem potest esse, ac finire. Sic in Computo judaico; ad obsignatam Mischna, ad obsignatum Thalmud, id est, finitum. Quod antea adduximus ex Marshamo. Porro quæ occultare & constanter è medio removere volumus, obsignamus, uti antea vidimus ex Dan. vi. 18. Matth. xxvii. 66. Unde obsignare idem est frequenter ac occultare. Denique quæ confirmare, ac firma rataque cupimus, sigillo notamus Ier. xxxii. 44. Unde obsignare idem est ac confirmare. Videamus jam, quomodo hæc huic loco applicari possint. Nempe sensus potest esse; ut finis imponatur prædictionibus de Christo venturo, sicut prophetia non amplius sit prophetia tanquam de futuro, sed testimonium tanquam de præsenti; & ministerium illud propheticum, quale olim fuit occupatum in promittendo Christo, prorsus cessaret, adeo ut post ejus adventum & passionem visio neque prophetes amplius esset, ut loquitur Tertullianus. Atque hoc modo non solum finitæ, sed & occlusæ, occultatæ, & quasi e medio remotæ sunt visio & prophetia; ut pateat inde, perinde esse, sive vox obsignare sensu finiendi, sive claudendi sumatur. Dein sensus esse potest; ut confirmentur, verificentur, rata, indubitataque veritatis comperiantur, per actualem scilicet impletionem, reique prædictæ exhi-bitionem, sicuti id quod obsignamus, firmum, ratum, verum esse declaramus. Apparet igitur, quovis modo etiam explice-mus obsignationem, & unde rationem ejus repetamus, ad impletionem prophetiarum, ante finem Lxx. hebdomadum expe-ctandam, atque in expiatione iniquitatis & justitiæ æternæ adduc-tione conspiciendam, hanc obsignationem referri debere.
units.tr: L. The angel further says that these prophetic visions are to be sealed. This word sealing has various meanings, according to the varied use and purpose of a seal. Writings that are finished are commonly sealed; hence to seal can mean the same as to finish. So in the Jewish reckoning: the Mishnah sealed, the Talmud sealed, that is, finished, as we cited earlier from Marsham. Again, what we wish to hide and constantly remove from sight we seal, as we saw earlier from Dan. VI. 18. and Matth. XXVII. 66. Hence to seal is often the same as to hide. Finally, what we wish to confirm and make firm and valid we mark with a seal (Jer. XXXII. 44.). Hence to seal is the same as to confirm. Let us now see how these senses can be applied to this passage. The meaning may be this: that an end is put to the predictions about the Christ who is to come, so that prophecy is no longer prophecy as concerning the future but testimony as concerning the present; and that prophetic ministry, such as once was employed in promising Christ, would wholly cease, so that after his coming and passion vision would no longer be prophecy, as Tertullian puts it. In this way vision and prophecy are not only finished but also closed, hidden, and as it were removed from sight, so that it is plain that it makes no difference whether the word to seal is taken in the sense of finishing or of closing. Again, the meaning may be this: that they are confirmed, verified, and found to be fixed, valid and true, namely by their actual fulfilment and the exhibition of the thing predicted, just as we declare what we seal to be firm, valid and true. It therefore appears that, however we explain the sealing, and from whatever source we derive its sense, this sealing must be referred to the fulfilment of the prophecies, which is to be awaited before the end of the seventy weeks, and to be seen in the expiation of iniquity and the bringing in of eternal righteousness.

units.la: LI. Observandum hoc contra Judæos. Notum est illud Thalmudicum; כל הנביאים כולן לא נתנבאו אלא לימות המשיח omnes omnino prophetæ non sunt vaticinati, nisi de diebus Messiæ. Atqui heic horum prædictiones de Messia implendas dicit Angelus intra Lxx. Septimanas, stante adhuc Urbe Sancta; ergo dudum impletæ sunt, quoniam Civitas illa jam à multis seculis diruta est, sanctaque esse desiit. Lubet ad majorem hujus rei confirmationem unum addere locum è Veteri Instrumento, in quo implementum prophetiarum de Christo, stante Templo Secundo, Civitateque sancta, futurum esse docetur. Huc refero Zach. viii. 3. 8. Sic dicit Iehovah: Reversus sum ad Tzionem, & habitabo in medio Hierosolyma, & vocabitur Hierosolyma עיר האמת Urbs Veritatis, & mons Iehovæ exercituum הר הקדש mons sanctitatis. Et adducam illos & habitabunt in medio Hierosolyma, & erunt mihi in populum, & ego ero ipsis in Deum, באמת ובצדקה in Veritate & justitia. Vulgò Judæi tradunt, Templum Secundum destitutum fuisse שכינה inhabitatione Dei super Arca. Non igitur illa umbratilis, sed illa σωματικὴ inhabitatio, per manifestationem Filii Dei in carne, intelligitur. Qua in carne ita habitavit Filius Dei, ut simul per eam habitaverit inter homines, potissimum inter suos, qui Hierosolymam spiritualem constituunt; imo etiam in Hierosolyma terrestri versatus passus sanguine conspersus sit, & ut ἰλαστήριον verum publicè omnium oculis expositus. Hanc ob causam urbs Hierosolyma tota יהוה כסא Solium Iehovæ, quod alias in Sancto sanctorum erat, vocari potuit Ier. iii. 17. imo Urbs Veritatis, ob exhibitum nempe Corpus omnium umbrarum, & signaculum omnium prophetarum, & Sion mons Sanctitatis, ob Sanctum Israelis corporaliter ibi præsentem. Quod ergò quia futurum erat, ideò Jehovah declarat se Deum populi fore, idque in veritate & justitia. Ad quæ verba Annotat. Belg. Ego certissime dabo ipsis, ipsis, quod promisi ipsis, & justificabo eos per Iesum Christum
units.tr: LI. This must be noted against the Jews. The Talmudic saying is well known: כל הנביאים כולן לא נתנבאו אלא לימות המשיח [kol ha-nevi'im kulam lo nitnabbe'u ela le-yemot ha-mashiach], all the prophets without exception prophesied only of the days of the Messiah. Yet here the angel says that their predictions about the Messiah are to be fulfilled within the seventy weeks, while the Holy City still stands; therefore they were long ago fulfilled, since that City has been destroyed for many centuries and has ceased to be holy. To add further confirmation of this matter, let me cite one passage from the Old Testament, in which it is taught that the fulfilment of the prophecies about Christ was to come while the Second Temple and the holy City still stood. To this I refer Zech. VIII. 3, 8: Thus says Jehovah: I have returned to Zion, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and Jerusalem shall be called עיר האמת [ir ha-emet], the City of Truth; and the mountain of Jehovah of hosts הר הקדש [har ha-kodesh], the mountain of holiness. And I will bring them, and they shall dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, בֶּאֱמֶת וּבִצְדָקָה [be-emet u-ve-tzedakah], in truth and righteousness. The Jews commonly teach that the Second Temple lacked the shekhinah, the indwelling of God above the Ark. Therefore it is not that shadowy indwelling but the bodily indwelling, σωματικὴ, through the manifestation of the Son of God in the flesh, that is meant. In that flesh the Son of God so dwelt that through it he also dwelt among men, above all among his own, who constitute the spiritual Jerusalem; indeed, while living in the earthly Jerusalem he suffered and was sprinkled with blood, and was publicly set forth before the eyes of all as the true propitiatory [ἱλαστήριον]. For this reason the whole city of Jerusalem could be called the throne of Jehovah יהוה כסא [kisse Yehovah], which otherwise was in the Holy of Holies (Jer. III. 17.); indeed, the City of Truth, on account of the body of all the shadows that was there displayed, and the seal of all the prophets; and the mountain of Holiness, on account of the Holy One of Israel bodily present there. Since this was to come, Jehovah therefore declares that he will be the God of his people, and that in truth and righteousness. On these words the Belgic Annotations say: I will most certainly give to them what I promised them, and justify them through Jesus Christ.

units.la: LII. Frustra ergò Judæi expectant impletionem prophetiarum de Messia, quæ ante vastationem Hierosolymæ fieri debuit, & verè facta est. Cujus rei testimonium quoque est abolitio sacrificii & muneris, de qua vers 27. Lex & prophetæ usque ad Johannem prophetarunt, non quod ille esset Messias, sed quod digito Messiam indicaret: Ecce agnus ille Dei, qui tollit peccatum mundi Joh. 1. 20. 26. 29. Hic est Iesus Nazarenus, in plenitudine temporis missus, de quo omnes Prophetæ Luc. 1. 69. 70. Act. III. 18. 24. VII. 52. uno ore locuti sunt; & in quo omnes promissiones Dei sunt τὸ ναὶ καὶ τὸ ἀμήν 2 Cor. 1. 20. & in quo veteres omnes prædictiones, & umbræ, veritatem habent Joh. 1. 14. 17. XIV. 6. Coll. II. 17. ac consummationem Joh. XIX. 30. Audiant Judæi, quod unus ex gente sua, vi veritatis pressus, de Jesu nostro dissimulare non potuit. Eodem tempore fuit Iesus, Vir sapiens, si tamen Virum cum fas sit dicere. Erat enim mirabilium operum patrator, & doctor eorum, qui libenter vera suscipiunt, plurimosque tam de Judæis, quam de gentibus sectatores habuit, Christus hic erat, quem accusatum a nostra gentis principibus Pilatus cum addixisset cruci, nihilominus non destiterunt diligere, qui ab initio caperant. Apparuit enim eis tertia die vivus, ita ut divinitus de eo Vates hoc & alia multa miranda prædixerant. Et usque in hodiernum diem Christianorum genus ab hoc denominatum non deficit. Ita Iosephus Antiquit Lib. XVIII. Cap. IV. Quæ verba Josephi, quibus Prophetas de Jesu nostro vaticinatos dicit, non necesse est, ut capiamus unice tanquam ex mente aliorum dicta; cum facile de Jesu, Viro ipsi illustri & Heroë, Prophetarum oracula prædixisse quædam credere potuerit. Uti & sic Vespasianum iis prænotatum asserit de Bell. Iud. Lib. VII. Cap. XII. Sed quod maxime eos ad bellum excitaverat, responsum erat ambiguum, itidem in sacris literis inventum, quod eo tempore quidam esset ex eorum finibus orbis terræ habituus imperium. Id enim illi quidem quasi proprium acceperunt, multique sapientes interpretatione decepti sunt. Hoc autem plane responso Vespasiani designabatur Imperium, qui apud Iudæam creatus est Imperator. Credibile est ad Mich. V. 1. respici.
units.tr: LII. The Jews therefore wait in vain for the fulfilment of the prophecies about the Messiah, which had to take place before the desolation of Jerusalem, and truly did take place. The abolition of sacrifice and offering, of which verse 27 speaks, is also a witness to this. The Law and the prophets prophesied until John (Luke XVI. 16.), not because he was the Messiah, but because he pointed to the Messiah with his finger: Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world (John 1. 20, 26, 29.). This is Jesus of Nazareth, sent in the fullness of time, of whom all the prophets (Luke 1. 69, 70.; Acts III. 18, 24.; VII. 52.) spoke with one voice; in whom all the promises of God are yea and amen (τὸ ναὶ καὶ τὸ ἀμήν, 2 Cor. 1. 20.); and in whom all the ancient predictions and shadows have their truth (John 1. 14, 17.; XIV. 6.; Col. II. 17.), and their consummation (John XIX. 30.). Let the Jews hear what a man of their own nation, pressed by the force of truth, could not conceal about our Jesus: About this time there lived Jesus, a wise man, if indeed one may call him a man. For he was a worker of wonderful deeds, and a teacher of those who gladly receive the truth; and he had many followers among both Jews and Gentiles. This was the Christ. When Pilate, on accusation by the leading men of our nation, had condemned him to the cross, those who had loved him from the beginning did not cease to do so. For on the third day he appeared to them alive again, just as the divine prophets had foretold this and many other wonderful things about him. And to this day the tribe of Christians, named after him, has not died out. So Josephus, Antiquities, Book XVIII, Chapter IV. We need not take Josephus's words, by which he says that the prophets prophesied about our Jesus, solely as expressions of the opinions of others; for he could well have believed that the oracles of the prophets foretold certain things about Jesus, an illustrious man and hero. Likewise he asserts that Vespasian was foreshadowed to them by these oracles, in The Jewish War, Book VII, Chapter XII: But what had most of all stirred them up to war was an ambiguous response, likewise found in the sacred writings, that at that time someone from their country would become ruler of the world. They took this as applying especially to themselves, and many wise men were deceived by this interpretation. Yet the response in fact pointed to Vespasian, who was made emperor in Judaea. It is credible that Mic. V. 1. is referred to here.

units.la: LII. Tandem ab effectis ad causam assurgit Angelus, etiam operis sui fructu & gloriâ nequaquam privandam; קדש קודש קדשים. Theodotio, καὶ ἐν χείσαι ἁγίων ἁγίων. Aquila ἁλείψαι ἡγιασμένον ἡγιασμένων. Vulgatus, ut ungatur Sanctus sanctorum. Ita & Tertullianus in masculino, quomodo & Græcæ Versiones accipi possunt. Clar. Coccejus; Veteres Masculine accipiunt. Sed קדש notat vel sanctitatem, vel sanctam rem. Est ergo hæc ρῆσις קדש קדשים vel abstractè Sanctitas Sanctitatum, vel in neutro, Sanctum Sanctorum, efferenda. Non est autem dubitandum, quin utroque modo de persona dici possit. Abstractum enim pro concreto poni frequens est 1 Sam. xxv. 6. Hagg. ii. 8. & genus neutrum de persona adhibetur in N. T. Matth. i. 20. Luc. i. 35. Joh. iii. 6. imo hæc ipsa vox קדש / sive abstractè, sive in neutro reddatur, de persona usurpatur Exod. xxviii. 36. Deut. xxxiii. 2. Ut adeò non malè Veteres vocem hanc masculine acceperint. Voluit tamen frequentior vocum harum usus, ut multi, non solum abstractè, vel in neutro eam transfuderint, quod & rectè factum, sed etiam rem, non personam, saltem primò & proprié, denotare crediderint. Scilicet de plurimis rebus, ad antiquam religionem pertinentibus, altari, v. g. vasis Tabernaculi, panibus propositionis, suffitu, munere, sacrificio pro reatu, omnibusque sacrificiis, prædicative usurpatur Exod. xxix. 37. xxx. 26. 29. 36. Levit. vi. 7. vii. 1. 6. x. 12. xiv. 13. xxiv. 9. Num. xviii. 9. subjectivè vero & absolutè enunciata (excepto uno aut altero loco Ezr. ii. 63. Neh. vii. 65.) ipsum Tabernaculi intimum recessum denotat Exod. xxvi. 33. 34. Heb. ix. 3. &c. dictum Sanctum Sanctorum, constructione Hebræis familiari, id est, sanctissimum. An autem nunquam sic latius usurpetur, pro aliis etiam Templi partibus, quod contendit aliquis, id strenuè affirmare non ausim; argumento loci Num. xvii. 10.
units.tr: LII. At last the Angel rises from the effects to the cause, since the fruit and glory of his own work must not be denied to him: [קדש קודש קדשים]. Theodotion: [καὶ ἐν χρίσει ἁγίων ἁγίων], and in the anointing of the saints of saints. Aquila: [ἀλεῖψαι ἡγιασμένον ἡγιασμένων], to anoint the sanctified of the sanctified. The Vulgate: that the Holy of Holies be anointed. So also Tertullian takes it in the masculine, as the Greek versions may also be taken. The illustrious Coccejus; the ancients take it as masculine. But קדש means either holiness or a holy thing. This expression קדש קדשים is therefore to be rendered either abstractly, Holiness of Holinesses, or in the neuter, Holy of Holies. Yet there is no doubt that in either way it can be said of a person. For an abstract noun is often used for a concrete one, 1 Sam. 25:6, Hagg. 2:8, and the neuter gender is applied to a person in the New Testament, Matth. 1:20, Luke 1:35, John 3:6. Indeed this very word קדש, whether rendered abstractly or in the neuter, is used of a person in Exod. 28:36 and Deut. 33:2. So the ancients were not wrong to take the word in the masculine. Still, the more frequent use of these words has led many to render it not only abstractly or in the neuter, which is also correct, but to believe that it denotes a thing and not a person, at least first and properly. Namely, it is used predicatively of many things pertaining to the ancient religion: of the altar, for example, the vessels of the Tabernacle, the showbread, the incense, the offering, the sin offering, and all sacrifices, Exod. 29:37, 30:26, 29, 36, Lev. 6:7, 7:1, 6, 10:12, 14:13, 24:9, Num. 18:9. But when stated subjectively and absolutely (except in one or two places, Ezra 2:63, Neh. 7:65), it denotes the innermost recess of the Tabernacle itself, called the Holy of Holies in the Hebrew manner of construction, that is, most holy, Exod. 26:33, 34, Heb. 9:3, etc. Whether it is never used more widely in this way, for other parts of the Temple as well, as someone contends, I would not dare to affirm strongly, on the strength of the passage Num. 17:10.

units.la: LIII. Volunt itaque quidam Templum materiale extruendum hic intelligi debere; sic ut קודש קדשים sive synecdochicè, sive latiori suo significatu totum Templum comprehendat et significet, Quando per unctionem ejus denotari credunt, vel consummationem ejus, per oblationem Christi futuram olim, cujus absque intuitu Templum habitaculum Dei, cultus in eo Deo exhibitus gratus ipsi, neque approbatus fuisset: vel consecrationem ejus per cultum Leviticum de novo instaurandum æ perficiendum, quando Christus, Unctus maximè, in eo apparens, cultum illum ab multiplici abusu purgaret, atque zelum suum in tuendâ loci majestate & sanctitate, per ejectionem hominum negotiantium, demonstraret Joh. 11. 14. 15. 16. Matth. XXI. 12. 13. Marc. XI. 15. 16. 17. Luc. XIX. 45. 46. Verum Daniel verf. 17. de Templo materiali loquens, ut & Angelus ipse verf. 16. aliud nomen adhibent nempe סקדש & קדש simpliciter. Vide etiam Cap. VIII. verf. 13. 14. XI. 31. Deinde oblatio Christi non fuit Unctio & sanctificatio Templi, sed verius abolitio ejus cum suppellectili sua. Quamvis enim ut futura hactenus considerata, Templo & sacrificiis praefigurantibus eam, sanctitatem & efficaciam quandam conciliabat; attamen jam praesens tollit umbras, easque inutiles, imo noxias declarat & efficit. Neque etiam nomine Unctionis consecratio Templi, per cultum de novo instaurandum, aut Christi in eo apparitio significari potest, quia expiatio peccati & justitiae aeternae adductio praemissa vetat omnino, ut de instauratione cultus ceremonialis, in hoc ultimo orationis membro, hujusque perfectione ac consummatione, Christo nempe cultum & Templum à prophanis abusibus vindicante & purgante, cogitemus. Quae etiam mortem Christi adeoque expiationem peccati antecessit, dum in hac Angeli Oratione eam sequitur Unctio Sancti Sanctorum.
units.tr: LIII. Some therefore wish the material Temple to be understood here, so that קודש קדשים, either by synecdoche or in its wider meaning, comprehends and signifies the whole Temple. They believe that by its anointing is meant its consummation through the future oblation of Christ, apart from the view of which the Temple, the habitation of God, and the worship offered to God in it, would not have been pleasing or approved to him. Or they take it as its consecration through the Levitical worship to be restored and completed anew, when Christ, the most Anointed, appearing in it, would cleanse that worship from its manifold abuse, and show his zeal for the majesty and holiness of the place by driving out the men who were trading, John 2:14, 15, 16, Matth. 21:12, 13, Mark 11:15, 16, 17, Luke 19:45, 46. But Daniel, speaking of the material Temple in verse 17, and the Angel himself in verse 16, uses another name, namely סקדש, and simply קדש. See also chapter 8, verses 13, 14, and 11:31. Further, the oblation of Christ was not the anointing and sanctification of the Temple, but rather its abolition, together with its furnishings. For although, considered as a future thing up to this point, it conferred upon the Temple and the sacrifices, which prefigured it, a certain holiness and efficacy, yet now that it is present it removes the shadows, and declares and makes them useless, indeed harmful. Nor can the consecration of the Temple through the worship to be restored anew, or the appearance of Christ in it, be signified by the word anointing, because the expiation of sin and the bringing in of eternal righteousness, which precede it, altogether forbid us to think of this in the last member of the sentence, namely the restoration of the ceremonial worship and its perfection and completion, with Christ cleansing and purging the worship and the Temple from profane abuses. Moreover, this anointing of the Holy of Holies, which in this speech of the Angel follows the death of Christ, and so the expiation of sin, would then have preceded it.

units.la: LIV. Alii Sanctum Sanctorum, non typicum & umbratile, sed verum intelligunt; hoc est, aliquid, vel id omne potius, quod olim per Sanctum Sanctorum praefiguratum fuit. Fuit autem primò typus summi Caeli. Quod docet Paulus, in genere non solum adstruens, quod Tabernaculum fuerit exemplar & umbra rerum caelestium Heb. VIII. 5. sed quod speciatim Sanctum Sanctorum fuerit antitypon Caeli, in quod ingressus Christus Heb. IX. 24. Unde ille caelum ingressus à Paulo dicitur ingressus esse Sanctuarium verf. 12. & ad dextram Dei sedens in caelis, Minister sanctuarii & veri Tabernaculi factus. Heb. VIII. 1. 2. Et ratio nomenclationis hujus est; quia Caelum est Dei Thronus Jef. LXVI. 1. ubi cum incredibili gloriae manifestatione habitat; atque sanctissimum illud Numinis palatium, quod pollutionem nullam aut polluti nihil admittit; in quoetiam sunt Arca, Propitiatorum, Cherubim &c. non typicè, sed verè Apoc. xi. 12. Hebr. xii. 22. 23. Jes. vi. 3. iu quo tandem Pontifex futurorum bonorum non sine sanguine proprio comparét, propitiationem semel factam sic in æternum consummaturus. Hoc ergo palatium Domini intelligendum esse heic contendunt cum Piscatore aliqui, quod cum ungendum dicat Angelus, illi de præparatione ac consecratione ejus ad cultum perfectissimum, illic à fidelibus consummatis Deo exhibendum, & factam per adscensionem Christi, id exponunt; sicuti olim Moses unxit Tabernaculi terrestris adytum, ut cultus ceremonialis illic perageretur. Exod. xl.
units.tr: LIV. Others understand the Holy of Holies not as typical and shadowy, but as the true one; that is, something, or rather everything, that was once prefigured by the Holy of Holies. It was first a type of the heaven above. Paul teaches this, asserting not only in general that the Tabernacle was a copy and shadow of heavenly things, Heb. 8:5, but specifically that the Holy of Holies was the antitype of heaven, into which Christ entered, Heb. 9:24. Hence he is said by Paul to have entered heaven as the one who entered the sanctuary, verse 12, and, sitting at the right hand of God in the heavens, to have been made minister of the sanctuary and of the true Tabernacle, Heb. 8:1, 2. And the reason for this naming is that heaven is the throne of God, Isa. 66:1, where he dwells with an incredible manifestation of glory; and it is that most holy palace of the Deity, which admits no pollution and nothing polluted. In it are also the ark, the mercy seat, the cherubim, and so on, not typically but truly, Rev. 11:12, Heb. 12:22, 23, Isa. 6:3. In it the High Priest at last appears, not without his own blood, of good things to come, about to bring to completion for ever the propitiation once made. Some with Piscator therefore contend that this palace of the Lord is to be understood here. Since the Angel says it is to be anointed, they explain this of its preparation and consecration for the most perfect worship, to be performed there by the faithful, now complete, to God, and made through the ascension of Christ. Just as Moses once anointed the inner sanctuary of the earthly Tabernacle, so that the ceremonial worship might be performed there, Exod. 40.

units.la: LV. Præterea notissimum est, Templum fuisse typum Ecclesiæ, hoc nomine ut & illis Domus Dei, & Habitaculi & Tabernaculi, ideò frequentissimè insignitæ Ps. xv. 1. xlvi. 5. Zach. vi. 12. 13. 2 Thess. ii. 4. 2 Cor. vi. 16. Ephes. ii. 21. 1 Tim. iii. 15. 1 Pet. ii. 5. imo & unius cujusque Fidelis 1 Cor. vi. 12. iii. 16. Ecclesia porrò vel est triumphans in cælis, vel militans in terris. Unde licet prior illa magis respondeat Sancto Sanctorum, & posterior Sancto; attamen & hæc, qualis est sub N. T. ad unum κεφαλαίωμα & similitudinem unius status cum cælesti illâ, in clariori cognitione mysteriorum salutis, majori libertate &c. adducta Ephes. i. 10. Heb. xii. 22. 23. Cant. i. 3. haud incommode nomine Sancti Sanctorum proponitur. Confert præcipuè Clar. Coccejus Ezech. xliii. 19. Hanc itaque Ecclesiam N. T. intelligunt alii, ungendam Spiritu largissime Joel ii. 28. conf. 2 Cor. i. 21. 1 Joh. ii. 23. 27.
units.tr: LV. Moreover, it is very well known that the Temple was a type of the Church, and for this reason it is most often called by the names House of God, Dwelling and Tabernacle, Ps. 15:1, 46:5, Zech. 6:12, 13, 2 Thess. 2:4, 2 Cor. 6:16, Eph. 2:21, 1 Tim. 3:15, 1 Pet. 2:5; indeed also of each single believer, 1 Cor. 6:19, 3:16. The Church is either triumphant in heaven or militant on earth. Hence, although the former corresponds more to the Holy of Holies and the latter to the Holy, yet the latter, as it is under the New Testament, brought to one recapitulation [κεφαλαίωμα] and a likeness of one state with that heavenly one, in clearer knowledge of the mysteries of salvation, with greater freedom, and so on, Eph. 1:10, Heb. 12:22, 23, Song 1:3, is quite fittingly set forth under the name of the Holy of Holies. Clarus Coccejus compares especially Ezek. 43:19. Others therefore understand this New Testament Church to be the one to be anointed most abundantly with the Spirit, Joel 2:28, compare 2 Cor. 1:21, 1 John 2:23, 27.

units.la: LVI. Tandem uti Tabernaculum & Templum, ita quam maximè ea Templi pars sanctissima, quæ Sanctum Sanctorum dicitur, fuit typus humanæ Christi naturæ. Sicuti enim Templum typus fuit rei omnis, in quo Deus speciali modo habitat, præsentemque se operationibus gratiosis & gloriosis declarat, qualis Cælum & Ecclesia est; ita certe typus debuit esse humanæ Christi naturæ, in qua plenitudo Deitatis habitat corporaliter Col. ii. 16. Inde est quod corpus suum Templum dixerit ipse Joh. ii. 19. ac Johannes, quod ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν Joh. i. 14. ac Jesaias, ipsum fore in Sanctuarium Jes. viii. 14. Id porrò facilè quivis animadvertit, quod, si Templum figura Christi fuerit, eâ sui parte quam maximè, quæ sanctissima erat, ac Numen intimè præsens habebat, qualis fuit adytum, humahumanam certe adumbrasse Christi naturam. Atque hoc modo rursus multi per Sanctum Sanctorum, Christum intelligunt, ejusque unctionem varie explicant, de qua posteà. Notandum denique, quod quidam hæc omnia jungant. Ita Polanus. Ista est sententia verborum Angeli. Ungetur Sanctum Sanctorum, hoc est, ungetur Christus Ecclesia ipsius & cælum, quæ per Sanctum Sanctorum, quod Moses unxit oleo sacræ unctionis fuerunt adumbrata. Clar. Coccejus jungit Christum & Ecclesiam, Caput ac corpus mysticum.
units.tr: LVI. Finally, just as the Tabernacle and the Temple were types, so above all that most holy part of the Temple, called the Holy of Holies, was a type of Christ's human nature. For just as the Temple was a type of everything in which God dwells in a special way and declares his presence by gracious and glorious operations, as heaven and the Church are, so it certainly ought to have been a type of Christ's human nature, in which the fullness of the Deity dwells bodily, Col. 2:9. Hence it is that he himself called his body a Temple, John 2:19, and John said that he dwelt [ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν] among us, John 1:14, and Isaiah that he would be a sanctuary, Isa. 8:14. Moreover, anyone can easily see that if the Temple was a figure of Christ, then especially that part of it which was most holy, and held God intimately present, namely the inner sanctuary, certainly foreshadowed Christ's human nature. In this way many again understand Christ through the Holy of Holies, and they explain his anointing in various ways, about which more later. It should finally be noted that some join all these together. Thus Polanus: This is the sense of the Angel's words: the Holy of Holies will be anointed, that is, Christ will be anointed, his Church and heaven, which were shadowed by the Holy of Holies that Moses anointed with the oil of holy anointing. Clarus Coccejus joins Christ and the Church, the Head and the mystical body.

units.la: LVII. Verum enim verò quando Angelus in sequentibus loquitur de Uncto, & de Uncto Principe, omninò judicandum est, illum sic explicasse amplius, quem per Sanctum Sanctorum ungendum intelligi volebat. Ille autem Princeps Unctus nullus alius est quam Filius Dei, promissus Redemtor Israelis. Referunt Gemaristæ de Ionathane filio Uzielis, qui Targum in Prophetas conscripsit, quod etiam tentaverit porro publicare Targum in Hagiographa, sed exiit בח קול / & dixit, sufficit Tibi, sed quares quia in iis est קץ משיח finis Messiæ, in Libro scilicet Danielis, ut fatetur Glossa. Vid. Augusti. Pfeiffer. Exercit. de Targ. Quæ rudera sunt Veteris interpretationis hujus Prophetiæ, quam jam penitus pervertunt Judæi recentiores, quamvis cæteroquin narratio hæc fabula mera sit. Neque enim finis Messiæ in libro Danielis tantum, sed & alibi, & præsertim Isef. LIII. memoratur. Si autem משיח נגיד est promissus Redemtor, uti est, ac in sequentibus amplius patebit, ergo & hoc Sanctum Sanctorum ungendum eundem denotare, non Cælum, non Ecclesiam, concludo; quia in hac Unctionis voce est allusio ad illud nomen Uncti, quod postmodum illi daturus erat Angelus.
units.tr: LVII. But when the angel goes on to speak of the Anointed and the Anointed Prince, it must be concluded that he was explaining more fully whom he meant to be anointed in the Holy of Holies. That Anointed Prince is none other than the Son of God, the promised Redeemer of Israel. The Gemarists report about Jonathan son of Uzziel, who wrote the Targum on the Prophets, that he also tried to publish a Targum on the Hagiographa, but a heavenly voice [בת קול] went out and said, "It is enough for you. Why do you search? For in them is the end of the Messiah [קץ משיח]", namely in the Book of Daniel, as the Gloss admits. See Augusti, Pfeiffer, Exercit. de Targ. These are the remains of the old interpretation of this prophecy, which the more recent Jews now entirely distort, although this story is otherwise pure fable. For the end of the Messiah is mentioned not only in the Book of Daniel but also elsewhere, especially in Isa. LIII. If, however, the Messiah the Prince [משיח נגיד] is the promised Redeemer, as he is, and as will become clearer in what follows, then I conclude that this Holy of Holies to be anointed denotes the same person, and not heaven or the Church, because in this word anointing there is an allusion to that title Anointed, which the angel was about to give him afterwards.

units.la: LVIII. Quin imò si verba hujus commatis modo ritè perpendantur, nulli, majori facilitate & emphasi, applicanda erunt, quam Christi soli. קרש קדשים masculinè capi potest, ut antè diximus, ac veteres acceperè, quando Sanctus Sanctorum est omnium Sanctissimus. Hoc Messiæ in veritate & plenitudine sensus quadrat; non tantum quia Deus est ter sanctus Isef. VI. 3. Sed & quia homo est nulla peccati labe unquam infectus. Ita eum descripsere vates. Non dabis חסידיך Sanctum tuum videre corruptionem Pf. XVI. 10. Pf. XLV. 8. Isef. LIII. 9. 11. Ier. XXIII. 5. Zach. IX. 9. &c. Ita & res se habet in Jesu nostro Actor. VII. 52. 1. Pet. III. 18. 1. Joh. II. 4. etiam ex confessione spiritus impuri Marc. 1. 23. Est verè sanctissimus & justissimus; absque omni nativâ peccati macula conceptus & natus Luc. 1. 35. Heb. VII. 26. vitam egit integerrimam 2. Cor. v. 21. Joh. VIII. 29. 46. amoremque Dei & proximi summum, in obedientia Patri præstita usque ad mortem crucis declaravit. Revera etiam hæc Sanctitas, omnibus numeris consummata requirebatur in Sacerdote, qui & victima, quæ expiaret peccata mundi; & in Sponsore, qui justitiam æternam peccatori adduceret, quæ non nisi perfectissimæ justitiæ addicta est per legem. Talis ergo nos decebat Pontifex &c. Heb. VII. 26.
units.tr: LVIII. Indeed, if the words of this clause are properly weighed, they can be applied to no one with greater ease and emphasis than to Christ alone. The phrase Qodesh Qodashim [קרש קדשים] can be taken in the masculine, as we said before, and as the ancients understood it, so that Holy of Holies means the most holy of all. This meaning fits the Messiah in truth and in fullness, not only because God is thrice holy, Isa. VI. 3., but also because the man is one never tainted by any stain of sin. The prophets described him thus: "You will not allow your Holy One [חסידיך] to see corruption", Ps. XVI. 10.; Ps. XLV. 8.; Isa. LIII. 9, 11.; Jer. XXIII. 5.; Zech. IX. 9., etc. So also the matter stands in our Jesus: Acts VII. 52.; 1 Pet. III. 18.; 1 John II. 4.; even by the confession of an unclean spirit, Mark I. 23. He is truly most holy and most just, conceived and born without any natural stain of sin, Luke I. 35.; Heb. VII. 26.; he lived a most blameless life, 2 Cor. V. 21.; John VIII. 29, 46.; and in obedience to the Father, even to the death of the cross, he showed the highest love of God and of neighbour. Indeed, this holiness, consummated in every respect, was also required in the priest, who was both the victim to expiate the sins of the world, and the surety who would bring eternal righteousness to the sinner, which is bound by the law to nothing short of the most perfect righteousness. Such a high priest was therefore fitting for us, etc., Heb. VII. 26.

units.la: LIX. Sed si קרש קרשים ad literam primò capere velimus de Templi adyto, certè & sub hac figura primariò Christus proponi meretur.
units.tr: LIX. But if we wish to take Qodesh Qodashim [קרש קדשים] first in the literal sense, of the inner sanctuary of the Temple, then certainly Christ is principally to be set forth under this figure as well.
